title: Conway's Game of Life
why: Four rules on a grid produce gliders, guns and even working computers. Nobody designed most of it; people found it.

title: Generative art
why: Artists write short programs and let randomness do the drawing. py5 lets you do it in Python.

title: Live-coded music
why: Sonic Pi turns code into sound as you type. People perform whole sets this way, on stage.

title: Build a computer from scratch
why: Nand to Tetris starts with a single logic gate and ends with a machine that runs Tetris.

title: Esoteric languages
why: Programming languages built as jokes, puzzles and art, including one written entirely in whitespace.

title: Advent of Code
why: Twenty-five small story puzzles every December, and every past year is still open to play.

title: Project Euler
why: Hundreds of maths puzzles that are painful by hand and satisfying with a short program.

title: Quines
why: Programs whose only output is their own source code. Writing one is a classic brain-teaser.

title: Rule 110
why: A one-line rule for colouring cells that turns out to be able to compute anything a computer can.

title: L-systems
why: A few rewriting rules grow convincing ferns, trees and snowflakes. Invented by a botanist.

title: The Mandelbrot set
why: One short formula, repeated, draws a shape with endless detail however far you zoom in.

title: Logo and the turtle
why: A 1960s language built so children could learn maths by steering a drawing robot.

title: PICO-8
why: A made-up 1980s-style console with tiny limits. People squeeze whole games into it.

title: The Nature of Code
why: A free book on simulating flocking, gravity and evolution with small programs.

title: Markov chains, visually
why: A playable explainer of the simple idea behind predictive text and weather models.

title: Crafting Interpreters
why: A free, friendly book that walks you through building your own programming language.

title: The demoscene
why: A subculture that makes music videos in real time, some from programs smaller than this page.

title: Code golf
why: A sport where the shortest program wins. The answers are unreadable and oddly beautiful.

title: Wave function collapse
why: An algorithm that grows whole towns and patterns from one tiny example image.

title: Boids
why: Three simple rules per bird are enough to make a convincing flock. Films have used it since the 1990s.
